title: Foundations of Stochastic Lexical Calculus: Semantic Descent and Random Dynamics on Probability Simplices
abstract: arXiv:2609.20207v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models produce prompt-dependent probabilities over words, whereas scientific systems require uncertainty over meaningful states that can be updated as evidence arrives. We develop an observable framework for determining when language-derived probabilities support such a sequential state representation. Theoretically, we define typed measurable transformations of contextual language, construct a minimal closed representation, and give necessary and sufficient conditions for semantic updates to exist uniquely. We bound irreducible nonclosure and accumulated error, and under average contraction prove existence, uniqueness and stability of an external random recursion on a probability simplex. These results define a stochastic lexical calculus without attributing an internal calculus to the language model. Empirically, frozen experiments test the observable implications. translated_title: 随机词汇演算的基础：概率单纯形上的语义下降与随机动力学
translated_abstract: 大语言模型产生的是依赖于提示词的词汇概率，而科学系统需要对有意义状态的不确定性建模，并随证据的到来而不断更新。我们开发了一个可观测的框架，用以判定何时由语言导出的概率能够支持这种序贯状态表示。在理论上，我们定义了上下文语言的类型化可测变换，构建了一个最小的闭表示，并给出了语义更新唯一存在的充要条件。我们界定了不可消除的非闭合性与累积误差，并在平均收缩条件下证明了概率单纯形上外部随机递归的存在性、唯一性与稳定性。这些结果定义了一种随机词汇演算，而无需将某种内部演算归因于语言模型本身。在实证方面，冻结实验检验了该理论的可观测含义。原始的提示条件概率未能通过预先指定的（测试）……
tldr: 本文建立了一个可观测的理论框架，给出了语言导出的概率能够唯一支持语义状态更新的充要条件，并在平均收缩条件下证明了概率单纯形上随机递归的存在性、唯一性与稳定性，从而构建了一种无需将内部演算归因于语言模型的随机词汇演算。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes an observable framework with necessary and sufficient conditions under which language-derived probabilities uniquely support semantic state updates, proving existence, uniqueness, and stability of random recursions on a probability simplex to define a stochastic lexical calculus without attributing an internal calculus to the language model.
